title: Gridheart
tagline: A pixel-art action roguelite where your health is a shape, and every weapon carves a different pattern out of it.
stateNote: A browser build you can play now. Expect a slice of the game, not a finished one.
problem: Health bars are a number. In Gridheart every character has a grid of health cells, and a weapon's shape is placed on that grid in the direction of the blow, so where you stand changes how much damage lands.
audience: Anyone who likes action roguelites and odd mechanics, and game developers curious about shape-based damage.
contribution: It is my project, made in Godot 4.3 and exported to the web. Weapons, armor plating and body-shape growth between rooms are the core mechanics.
worksToday: A sword, spear, hammer, axe, dagger and bow each take a different pattern from the target's grid.
After a room you choose a growth shape, rotate it and attach it to your own grid.
Mouse, keyboard aim and attack-in-direction controls all work, and you can switch mid-fight.
limitations: It is a slice of a game. Content and balance are still changing.
I checked that the hosted build loads, not every room or weapon.

involve.headline: Play it and tell me where it breaks.
asks: Tell me which weapon felt best and which felt pointless.
If you make pixel art or design combat, I'd like to hear what you'd change.
